item.description:
**Fieldbook 2.4.4 beta 5** (a beta)
### Changed - **Deleting a customer or label with meetings:** after asking, it moves to the Trash whole, with its meetings, labels, account notes, files, and emails, and **Put Back** returns it whole. Before, only empty ones could be deleted. - **Speaker voice data** of a deleted meeting is kept while it's in Fieldbook's Trash, so a meeting put back still matches its speakers; it's deleted when the meeting leaves the Trash. - **Shorter AI settings:** under **Service**, one line says where meeting text goes; the full list is folded under **What's sent**. Each service's note is shorter too. - **File Transfers › Your Devices:** a Mac pairs here as well as an iPhone or iPad, so the button is now **Pair a Device…**, and **Settings › General › Sync with paired devices** turns it off.
### Added - **Fieldbook's own Trash:** deleted meetings go to **Trash**, last under Library in the sidebar, instead of the macOS Trash. Each one shows its days left; **Put Back** returns it to its label or folder (or Unfiled if that's gone), and **⋯ › Delete Now** and **Empty Trash…** move items on to the macOS Trash. After 30 days they go there by themselves. - **New meetings from your other Mac, when you add them:** with another Mac paired, meetings made there are listed on this Mac (**From Mac** in the toolbar, the Dock icon, the menu-bar menu, and File Transfers) with **Add**, **Not Now**, and **Don't Add**. Nothing joins your library by itself. Added meetings come without audio, filed where they were, and the other Mac moves its own copy to the Trash. - **Change another Mac's meetings from this one:** with another Mac paired, your notes, titles, dates, folders, to-dos, and speaker names changed here go back to it at the next sync. The meeting says how many changes are waiting, and a small clock marks it in the list. If both Macs changed the same thing, notes and to-dos keep both; for the rest the other Mac keeps its own, and the meeting offers **Use Mine** or **Dismiss**.
### Fixed - With another Mac's meetings shown, search no longer rebuilds its index for them at every launch.

**Fieldbook 2.4.4 beta 4** (a beta)
### Changed - **Another Mac's accounts show too:** a customer only the other Mac has opens with its account notes, account summary, opportunities, MEDDPICC, and issues, read-only, marked **From <Mac> · read-only here**; writing or changing them is greyed out. - **Another Mac's notes can be selected and copied:** your notes and the email draft of the other Mac's meetings are read-only but no longer greyed out as a whole. - **Right-click on another Mac's meetings:** Move To, About, Archive, New Reminder, Change Date and Time, Merge, and Move to Trash are greyed out; Open, Find or Ask, Show in Finder, Export, and Send stay.
### Fixed - Closing the Pair with Another Mac sheet stops looking for the other Mac at once.

**Fieldbook 2.4.4 beta 3** (a beta)
### Added - **The Mac stays awake while Fieldbook records or transcribes:** an in-person meeting on battery no longer ends when the Mac's sleep timer runs out. The display can still go to sleep; closing the lid or choosing Sleep still sleeps the Mac. - **Another Mac's meetings, read-only:** pair a second Mac (Settings › General › Another Mac › Pair…, typing the code the first Mac shows in File Transfers › Pair iPhone or iPad…), and it shows every meeting from the first Mac, with notes, AI notes, transcripts, and accounts, beside its own. Never audio or voices. They sync while Fieldbook is open on both, on the same network; change them on the Mac they came from. - **Help: Connecting Outlook or Google Calendar:** step by step, adding your work calendar to the Mac through System Settings › Internet Accounts, and what to do on a managed Mac.

Offered to 1.8 and later as an automatic update, a small one from 2.4.2. Everything in the four betas of 2.4.3: echo reduction off by default, Search on its own page, Find & Ask in a meeting, Join and Record from Today, better titles and transcripts, and Meeting Time that can count meetings you accepted.
### Added - **Join and Record:** in Today, Join's arrow (and the right-click menu) offers **Join and Record**: it opens the meeting link and starts recording, named and filed from the invite, in one click. - **Better titles without a calendar event:** a meeting named "Meeting", "Zoom call", or "Notes" and the date gets a short title from its first AI notes, such as "Contoso pricing review", in the same AI request. Titles you typed and calendar titles are never changed. - **"This meeting looks over"**: when a recording linked to a calendar event has no call app to follow, Fieldbook asks once whether to stop when the event ended 5 minutes ago and both sides have been quiet for a minute. It never stops on its own. - **Is this the other invitee?** In a 1:1, when one person on the call side is still unnamed and only one invitee is left, Fieldbook offers that invitee's name with Yes and No. - **Help and Settings in the sidebar:** at the bottom, under My To-dos, as in Fieldbook for Windows. - **Help: your calendar through a private iCal link**, for when your company won't let you add your work account to this Mac.
### Changed - **Echo reduction is off by default:** with it on, some call apps (Teams in a browser, for one) could hear you much more quietly. If you picked a setting before, it's kept. Turn it on in the Recorder's microphone menu or Settings › General › Microphone. - **Search has its own page:** click **Search** in the sidebar, above Library, or press Shift-Command-F. One big box finds words in your meetings as you type and asks AI when you press Return, with a menu to search one folder and a switch to include the archive. Your recent questions are under it. The search field and the **Ask** button are gone from the toolbar. - **Find & Ask in a meeting:** the new magnifying-glass button at the top right of a meeting (or Command-F) opens a column that lists the meeting's lines matching what you type, and asks AI about the meeting when you press Return. - **Opportunity and Issues** are higher in a meeting's header, under its folder and above the date, where they're easier to see. - **Meeting Time counts meetings you accepted but didn't record:** the setting is now **Count accepted meetings you didn't record** (Settings › Meetings › Calendars). With it on, a meeting you accepted or organized counts even without a recording, with the invite's length; a tentative invite counts only when you record it, import it, or add notes. Each week in Meeting Time says how many it has that you didn't record, marks them **accepted · not recorded**, and has **Add Notes…** beside each. - **Transcripts:** company names of a meeting's invitees (from their email addresses) are spelled right more often, and Whisper's stray “Subtitles by…” and “Thanks for watching” lines are left out where nobody was speaking. - **Ask AI:** answers from small and local models no longer show leaked reasoning, “Based on the provided sources” openings, or a pile of citations in one group. - **New calendar events show sooner:** Fieldbook asks macOS to sync your calendars before reading them, at most once a minute. - **Your iPhone and iPad use your fiscal year:** the fiscal year start you set on the Mac now syncs, so quarters on the iPhone and iPad match the Mac's.
### Fixed - **Update All:** checks what’s out of date in the background, so the app no longer pauses on a library in a synced folder such as Google Drive. - **Issues:** the page responds quickly while typing, opening issues, and changing severity or status. - **Speakers:** names no longer get cut off on a narrow page; status moves under the name.

Offered to 1.8 and later as an automatic update, a small one from 2.4.1. Everything in the six betas of 2.4.2: import recordings from other recorders and calls, hear a speaker before naming them, tag a meeting with its opportunity and issues while you record, Meeting Time that counts the meetings you attended, and update checks that try again.
### Added - **Import recordings:** the **Import** button and **File › Import Recording or Transcript…** now take audio and video files (MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, AIFF, FLAC, CAF, MP4, MOV, M4V), such as recordings from Plaud, Pocket, and other recorders, or Zoom and Teams recordings. Each becomes a meeting, transcribed on your Mac with its speakers found, like your own recordings. Only the sound is kept. You can also drag them into Fieldbook, onto a folder, or use **File › Add Files…**. - **Offer to add audio and video you download** (Settings › General › Downloads and Email Folder): an audio or video file you download or AirDrop while Fieldbook is open asks where it goes, as a downloaded email does. Nothing is added without asking. - **Hear who a speaker is before naming them:** click a speaker's name and **Listen** plays one of their paragraphs, then stops; the arrows go to their others. **Show All** opens a find bar under the player that steps through everything they said in the transcript, marked in their color, with **Play** and **Name…**.
### Changed - **Tag a meeting while you record:** the **Opportunity** and **Issues** menus are at the top of the meeting, under its date, so you can tag a customer call with its opportunity and issues during the call. They used to appear beside the **Brief** only once the AI notes were written. - **Meeting Time counts the meetings you attended:** the ones you recorded, imported, or took notes for, in every week and year, past ones included. Your calendar still files and times them. To also count calendar meetings you didn't record, as before, turn on **Count calendar meetings you didn't record** in **Settings › Meetings › Calendars**. - **Recordings from your iPhone or iPad, and imported recordings:** nobody is labeled you any more, since the person who talks most isn't always you. Name yourself like anyone else; with **Remember this voice**, Fieldbook recognizes you in later ones. Recordings made on your Mac are unchanged. - **Importing a recording** refuses a file whose sound is kept in other files it points to (a QuickTime reference movie): Fieldbook reads only the file you chose. Export it as one file, such as MP4 or M4A, and import that. - **Ask about one meeting:** the question field is at the top of the column, under its title, and ready to type in as soon as the column opens. Follow-ups go in the same field, and each new answer scrolls into view. - **Search:** the results start with **Results for “…”** and an **✕** that closes the search and brings back the folder's meetings. Esc does the same.
### Fixed - **Updates:** when the daily update check can't reach the update server, for example because your Mac just woke and isn't back on the network yet, it now tries again up to three times, an hour apart. It used to wait a whole day. - **Meeting lists:** in **All Meetings**, **Archive**, and a customer's **Also about**, a meeting's folder path always shows in full and a long title is cut off at its end, instead of drawing over other text. A customer whose only meetings are under **Also about** no longer shows "No meetings here" over one of them. - **Pre-call briefs:** when a recording is switched to another meeting at the same time, it no longer keeps the first meeting's brief (with that customer's agenda, invitees, and history). It gets the other meeting's brief instead, if there is one. The first meeting's brief stays ready for that meeting. - **View › Show Source Times** (Option-Command-T) now works at the standard text size; it was greyed out unless the text was bigger or smaller, and **Actual Size** wasn't greyed out at actual size. - **Diagnostics:** an alert left open, such as "An error occurred in retrieving update information", is no longer logged as the app not responding.

Offered to 1.8 and later as an automatic update, a small one from 2.4. Everything in the four betas of 2.4.1: ask about one meeting, recent questions, talk time, stakeholders, and accounts on your iPhone and iPad.
### Added - **Ask about one meeting:** click **Ask** in the toolbar with a meeting open, and a column beside it answers questions about that meeting only, from its transcript, your notes, its AI notes, and its attached files. Cited times open the line beside the conversation. - **Recent questions:** your Ask AI questions and their answers are kept on this Mac for 90 days. Open one again without asking the AI, continue it, or ask it again; matching ones show under **Asked before** as you type in the search field. Turn it off, or clear them, in **Settings › AI**. A meeting moved to the Trash takes its questions with it. - **Talk time:** a meeting's **Speakers** list shows each person's share of the talk time with a bar, and each side's share under the heading (for example **Internal 52% · Customer 32% · Partner 12% · No side 4%**), so you can see who talked most and least. - **Stakeholders:** in Sales mode, a customer or partner meeting's AI notes have a **Stakeholders** section: each person's stance on your solution (**Champion**, **Supporter**, **Neutral**, or **Detractor**), why, and their own words. Someone talked about but not in the meeting shows who reported it. Each customer's **Account** page lists everyone with a name from its meetings, with their side, their stance now and before, and how often they came up and talked; open a person for their stance in each meeting. Speakers not yet named ("Speaker 1") show in their meeting's notes, and join the Account page once you name them in the transcript, with no new AI request. **Add Stakeholders…** there reads the last 90 days' meetings from before this, with the quick tasks model. Stances are for you: they stay out of Copy and emails. - **Accounts on your iPhone and iPad:** each customer's **Account** page now goes to your paired iPhone and iPad with each sync, to read: open opportunities with their amounts and links, account notes, the summary with its executive part, open conflicts, customer status, and the detailed summary. Tap a statement's quote mark to see where it came from. In General mode, each **Folder Summary**. Customers with no recent meeting come too. Nothing on the device changes it: change it on your Mac, and it follows with the next sync. With Fieldbook for iPhone build 22 or later.
### Changed - **About** works while a meeting is recording or being transcribed, like Move To. Move it to Internal or Partners, then pick the customers it's about; its notes are marked for them once they're written.
### Fixed - **Spreadsheets** (in Files, customer reports, and the licensing library) reach the AI with their dates, percentages, and amounts (2025-11-01, 25%, $1,234.50) instead of raw numbers such as 45962 or 0.25. - **Pasting into notes** from a browser or other app keeps curly quotes, apostrophes, dashes, and accented letters, instead of turning them into symbols such as â€œ and â€™. - **About** on an Unfiled meeting: its greyed-out button now says to move the meeting to Internal or Partners first, instead of calling it a customer meeting. - **Narrow windows and larger text:** in **File Transfers**, the **Your iPhone and iPad** heading puts its description and **Pair iPhone or iPad…** under the title instead of running past the page's edge, and on a customer's **Account** page, **Add Stakeholders…** goes under its heading at larger text sizes, as **Check for Conflicts** does.
